title: Musicians he enjoyed: Willie Humphrey, Benny Allen, Jerry Green
summary: He praises his 1937 band and tells how it won at St. Monica's.

bands.name: Clyde Kerr and William Houston's band

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: Who were the musicians that you really enjoyed playing and you think were really good?

Well, musicians I enjoyed playing with like Russ, Willie Humphrey, now Willie Humphrey come back here. They come back here and if you want to use a stick, I said, no, don't worry about the planet and get on the alto. So he got on the alto and started working that. I said, we got two of them. I said, we're going back there to St. Monica's, they got all them hells back there but we're going to give them religion tonight when we go back there. And the number when I played back there, just said come out, just before intermission we played it, Slow Boat to China. You understand me? That number just said come out, Slow Boat to China. We played that number. We swung this other number, Stomp at the Savoy. We swung that and then we swung the sunny side of the street. That's where Lionel's Crip. And then we swung that and then we swung the sunny side of the street. That's where Lionel's Crip. And Benny sounded like Art Tatum at times and Earl Hines. Benny. Benny Allen, he was big, he was Keeto's cousin. He lived in a great time. He died. Oh man he could play some bouncing. Oh talk about the piano. And Jerry Green, well Jerry Green had been with Clyde Carr and Houston with them big old Lion bands you know, he'd come over there with us with that bass and I had, he'd come over there with us and I had, he'd come over there with us and I had, he'd come over there with them, you know straighten them licks shorter on the bass and pray a bass and don't make a gang of noise, you understand what I mean? Play smooth. You see all that staccato, that wasn't easy, we need that legato, the smoothness, you understand what I mean? And that's where we went, that's where we stole the show with them people. Them people said, all them raggedy drummers, musicians, they can't play out all them guys, all dressed up, looking like Clark Gable. Yeah. Homie G was back there with that bass. He was with Henry Horton. Listen, all this stuff I'll tell you about, open confession is good for the soul, they'll tell you. Poor Jew and Garth, but we give religion, all the bad boys. I don't know if Garth must have got his lips fired down that night because he was a good musician too. He was piano playing and everything. Did you ever meet him? Never. I never met him twice. Yeah, Gladys.

I had some bad boys playing with me. I had some bad boys playing with me. And well that's right, all of them could play. I wouldn't hide nobody. See, Carl and them, they wanted to be the outstanding guy. I didn't care how much you played, as long as you played right. You understand what I mean? Of course now people like in these late years like George Lewis and them, well they come about like cuckoos and that bunch come about. Well the times that I'm telling you about these fellas, they was good musicians in their time but they couldn't touch it. Like Hugh Albert and all that, he got trouble with the Tawana bass, that ain't nothing but like them old time guys, ta They used to play that a long time ago, yeah.
